goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — The add/remove mutation promises detach the follow-up refresh, so callers report success before the UI reload finishes and refresh failures become unhandled.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js, both removeMember and addMembers return the promise from Discourse.ajax(...).then(...), but inside the `then` callback they call `self.findMembers();` without returning it. That means callers observing the returned promise will see it resolve as soon as the mutation request succeeds, not when the subsequent refresh finishes. Any failure from findMembers() is also not chained, making it effectively unhandled by the caller. This behavior is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:35 — Pagination commits the new offset before the request succeeds, so a failed request labels the old member list as the new page.

adjudication.rationale:
In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `next` and `previous` actions compute a new `offset`, immediately call `group.set("offset", offset)`, and then trigger `group.findMembers()`.

`currentPage` is computed from `offset/limit`, while the displayed member list comes from `group.members` which is only updated in the `then` of the AJAX call inside `findMembers`. If the AJAX request fails/rejects, there is no error handling to roll back `offset`, so the UI can reflect the new page number (`currentPage`) while still showing the old `members` list (since it was not updated). This mismatch is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:30 — Concurrent member fetches are not sequenced, allowing a slower stale response to overwrite a newer page or post-mutation refresh.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers()` issues an async `Discourse.ajax(...)` and, on resolution, unconditionally `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members })` on the group. The diff also adds multiple call sites that can trigger overlapping requests (e.g., admin controller `next`/`previous` actions call `group.findMembers()` after updating `offset`, and `addMembers`/`removeMember` call `self.findMembers()` in a `.then`). There is no request sequencing (token/check of expected `offset`), cancellation, or “latest request wins” guard, so a slower earlier request can resolve after a later one and overwrite the newer `offset/members` state with stale data, producing incorrect pagination/member list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - — Automatic-group protection (`return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic`) is present and correctly applied to both new `add_members` and `remove_member` actions, consistent with `update`/`destroy`; no bypass found there

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding does not point out a defect; it explicitly states the automatic-group protection is present and correctly applied with no bypass. In the diff, both `add_members` and `remove_member` do include `return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic`, consistent with `destroy`, and `update` prevents renaming automatic groups. Since it identifies no bug/security/correctness issue introduced by the change, it is not a real problem finding.
